descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · TFA-94422 AC 7; UAT 3.5 · “The full retry sequence stays within ~30 s”.

Decision D8 · S2 · Daniela

Should In Today reset at server midnight; the worst-case AI wait is ~38 s (UAT says ~30 s); measured 2026-10-15 with both models hanging: Ask AI gives up at 30.0 s, but the pre-round summary only at 62.5 s (its sub-calls go through the 30 s retry sequence twice), past the case's 60 s limit (EFS/S21)

Note: Measured 2026-10-16 on 25acd727 (OAT-03/S09, S11): Generate with both models hanging gives up at 30.0 s (1.0 s when both return 429); Ask AI with Haiku hanging is answered by Mistral at 20.0 s.

Other cases of the same question (counted once): TC-09/S13, EFS/S21

Approach · TC-14 In-Room Dictation & Note Generation · S21 The full retry sequence stays within about 30 s

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • T9 The full retry sequence stays within about 30 s. (TFA-94422 AC 7; UAT 3.5)
  • U15 Generate timing: each run logs how long the AI call itself took, separately from the total; any run over 30 s where the AI service was not the cause is reviewed with Vikram. … (UAT 3.5)

Test design technique: Performance (performance) — Measure the time and check it is within the required seconds.

Given convex/ai/providers/retry.ts on main: CALL_BUDGET_MS 30000, ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS 20000, MIN_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS 8000, RETRY_DELAY_MS 1000, RETRY_PRIMARY_IF_FAILED_WITHIN_MS 10000; unit tests e2e/unit/provider-retry.unit.ts (RT-07, RT-08)

When Review the budget code and the unit test results for slow Haiku, slow retry, and a fallback that starts late

Then Haiku, its retry and the Mistral fallback together finish or fail within about 30 s, and the fallback always gets at least 8 s. Computed worst case on main: a temporary Haiku failure at just under 10 s, the 1 s pause, a second Haiku try capped at the remaining 19 s, then the 8 s Mistral floor: about 38 s. …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Doc review against TFA-94422 AC 7, judged on the computed worst case (about 38 s), not on RT-08 alone: RT-08 checks that each deadline comes from the remaining budget but does not model the slow-first-failure path. Whether about 38 s is 'about 30 s', and whether skipping the retry after a slow temporary failure meets AC 2, is Q22. …

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method CODEREVIEW · Code review; lane planned in the matrix: manual (manual)

S21 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-14.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row; to be decided by Daniela; the Allure status was changed by the triage from passed to failed.

Issue type: Needs a decision (Daniela) · environment local · tickets TFA-94422 ready for qa

In the worst case (Haiku fails temporarily just under 10 s, then its retry times out), the physician waits about 38 s, not about 30 s, before the Mistral note or an error appears.

Evidence: Allure 13500983, code-review fail-pending-Q22. From retry.ts: 9.99 s + 1 s pause + 19 s retry + 8 s Mistral floor ≈ 38 s. The fallback always gets at least 8 s. TC-14 matrix Q22 is open: is 38 s 'about 30 s' under TFA-94422 AC 7, and does skipping the retry after a slow temporary failure meet AC 2? Not in the dev report or ledger.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: CODEREVIEW · Code review; secondary: UNIT · Unit test — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: newspec-c.
